title: a proof that launches a scratch-HOME ground loop leaves none alive after it exits, run through the tester or plainly
intention: A scratch HOME reaps the ground loop launched under it when the proof that made it exits, so no ground_loop whose HOME is a scratch dir outlives its proof and no scratch run.lock stays held, whether the proof ran through the tester or plainly; the house HOME's loop is never touched.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akienyoga9i by akienyoga9i_cc_0 with the Restart Manager (read-only): 56 ground_loop pythonw processes, 28 parent/child pairs; only the house pair (5168/16420) is legitimate, the other 27 children each hold a stale scratch HOME's run.lock under %TEMP%, from proofs of ae0d88a55edb, 42ddfe3b7256 and 4356ea1d8755. Causes measured: windowless_spawn's detached child stays in run_owned's job (killed 2 s after return); every orphan's tree had 715d2205a2ec's fix; the tester's run_proof log shows none of those proofs ran through it at any orphan's start. So proofs run outside run_owned leak their scratch loops.
traces_to: Law 7 (a leaked process holding a lock is a silent error); CP6 (safety built, not assumed); outline 9.4.2 (the tester's runs leave nothing behind) extended to plain runs.
how: In the scratch HOME's teardown (or the builder's chosen site), read the scratch HOME's ground_loop run.lock holder and end it with its child before the HOME is removed. A red-first proof launches a scratch-HOME ground loop from a plain subprocess, lets it exit, and finds no ground_loop with that HOME alive.

clauses.claim: a proof that launches a scratch-HOME ground loop and exits, run plainly (not through run_owned), leaves no ground_loop alive whose HOME is that scratch dir, and its run.lock is not held
the same proof run through bin/cairn test leaves none alive either
the house HOME's ground loop is alive and holds its run.lock after both runs

decisions.text: D1: the scratch HOME's teardown reaps the ground loop (and its child) holding that HOME's run.lock, only for a scratch HOME.
D2: one red-first proof, one tooth per clause; the plain-run tooth measures on Windows and on Linux.
D3: the scratch charter's what and proof name the reap (scratch_dir's removal first ends what still holds the directory) and its proof, because a tool's charter says what its public interface does.
